points.description: States that the time-area method is used in hydrologic routing / to derive a runoff hydrograph from rainfall input (storm intensity vs time curve, i.e. hyetograph).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it produces a runoff hydrograph or is a routing method, without linking to rainfall hyetograph/intensity-time input.

points.description: States that it is significant for larger catchments because it accounts for processes/contributions of smaller sub-regions (areas) individually.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it suits large catchments, or only says it considers sub-areas, without linking the two.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for stating that the method generates runoff hydrographs from the rainfall hyetograph (hydrologic routing) and that it matters for large catchments because sub-areas are treated individually. Give part marks for a vague or half-stated version of either idea. Give no marks for unrelated or wrong statements, e.g. describing it as a method for something other than runoff hydrograph generation.
